name: Philip Hager
forbes_bio: Philipp Hager is a major shareholder of Hager SE.
The company is a leading provider of solutions and services for electrical installations, covering business fields such as energy distribution, cable management, and building automation.
Hager SE generates consolidated group revenues exceeding $3.5 billion annually.
Originally founded as a GmbH, the company has a history spanning over three decades and transitioned into a Societas Europaea (SE) in May 2007.
The group operates internationally with a workforce exceeding 13,000 employees and manages well-known brands such as Hager, Berker, and E3/DC.

name: Jason Gardner
sec_insider_companies: Marqeta, Inc. (MQ) - Director,TenPercentOwner; Pagaya Technologies Ltd. (PGY) - Director
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Hurun Global (2022); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Jason Gardner is the founder and CEO of Marqeta, a fintech company that helps companies issue debit cards.
A New Jersey native, Gardner spent his high school years working at a thrift store and selling t-shirts on the trains to Grateful Dead concerts.
He built a rent payment startup that he sold to financial firm MoneyGram in 2007 for $28 million.
In 2010 he founded Marqeta, which created an API that allows companies like DoorDash and Square to issue debit cards.
The $290 million (2020 revenue) business processed 1.6 billion transactions in 2020 across some 57 million active cards.
forbes_facts: Gardner attended Arizona State University and worked as an assistant to Senator John McCain in his 20s.

name: Rafal Brzoska
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Rafał Brzoska is the founder and CEO of InPost, a logistics company that operates over 11,000 parcel lockers in Poland.
Brzoska started out by founding Integer Group, which distributed leaflets, in 1999
Seven years later, he started InPost, which operates automated lockers that allow customers to drop off and collect packages at any time of the day.
The company went public in Amsterdam in 2021, raising over $3 billion in its IPO.

name: Subba Rao Jasti
forbes_bio: Patriarch Subba Rao Jasti's wealth comes from his stakes in listed Suven Pharmaceuticals and Suven Life Sciences as well as a November 2021 sale of shares to global private equity player Advent.
Suven was founded in 1989 by his son Venkateswarlu Jasti and went public in 1995.
The Hyderabad company was demerged in 2020 into Suven Pharmaceuticals, which does contract research and Suven Life Sciences, which focuses on neuroscience therapies.
In November, the Jastis sold the bulk of their stake in listed flagship Suven Pharma to global private equity player Advent International. They still retain a 10% holding.
forbes_facts: His daughter-in-law Sudharani is a director on the board of Suven Life Sciences.
His son ran a chain six of community pharmacies in the state of New York and New Jersey in the United States in the 1970s and 1980s.

name: Vladimir Leschikov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2019-2021); Hurun Global (2020)
forbes_bio: Vladimir Leschikov owns more than 370 acres of land near the border between Moscow and New Moscow territory.
That's where his shopping complex Slavyanskiy Mir (Slavic world), with a space of about 3 million square feet, is located.
Leschikov was born in Dagestan in the North Caucasus region.
Leschikov and his older brother moved to Moscow bought rooms in the center of Moscow to lease them.
Moscow's government plans to build two metro stations on Leschikov's land.

name: Wenjun Dai
forbes_bio: Dai Wenjun chairs Juewei Food, a supplier of duck necks and braised duck parts through a retail chain across China.
Juewei went public at the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2017.
Dai holds an EMBA from the Cheung Kong Business School in Beijing.
Juewei is headquartered in the southern Chinese city of Changsha.

name: Jasminder Singh
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2021); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun India (2015-2018); Sunday Times Rich List (2020); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Hotelier Jasminder Singh's Edwardian Hotels London group owns 12 high-end hotels in London and Manchester, including The May Fair Hotel.
Singh purchased his first hotel, The Edwardian, in 1975 for about $750,000.
In 1993 he partnered with Radisson; 11 of the group's hotels are now branded Radisson Blu Edwardian.
The group's $400 million luxury development at Leicester Square, The Londoner hotel, opened in the fall of 2021.
Singh's wife, Amrit, son, Inderneel, and daughters, Siraj and Krishma, all hold senior positions with Edwardian Hotels London.
forbes_facts: Singh grew up in Tanzania and Kenya before moving to the UK and qualifying as an accountant.
Singh's father took him to court in 2012 claiming part of his son's fortune under Sikh culture of sharing wealth among generations. The court ruled for Jasminder.

name: Ravi Puravankara
forbes_bio: Ravi Puravankara is the founder chairman of Bangalore-based real estate firm Puravankara.
A farmer's son, Puravankara got into real estate when he was still in college.
The company has completed 86 residential and commercial projects across 9 cities in India.It has a land bank of 36 million square feet, the bulk of which is under development.
His U.S.-educated son, Ashish, runs the company the managing director.
It has an interior design arm called Purva Streaks and a construction outfit called Starworth Infrastructure and Construction.
